title: Off-Register Riso — Small Press Chapbook
description: A two-color risograph zine page built for poetry introductions, with deliberate misregistration, large-dot halftones, and photocopied type that feels pulled straight from a staple-bound chapbook.
philosophy: This template enshrines the productive failures of small-press printing — the ghost offset of a second riso ink pass, the coarse halftone screen that turns a face into a field of dots. It actively refuses digital smoothness, treating misalignment and contrast loss not as bugs but as the entire point. It is built for creators who understand that a blurry photocopy carries more conviction than a 4K export, and for audiences who will lean in closer because the imperfection signals authenticity. The presenter this template belongs to has a shelf of staple-bound zines and knows the smell of risograph ink.
goodFor: Poetry chapbook introductions and author title pages
Small-press launch announcements with deliberate lo-fi aesthetic
3-line pull quotes set in distressed or blurred display type
Zine-culture events, art-book fairs, and indie literary readings
avoidFor: Data-heavy slides requiring legible charts, tables, or fine labels
Client-facing decks where brand polish and consistency are mandated
Large projected rooms with low-contrast or washed-out display environments
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a cover pulled from a staple-bound poetry chapbook — raw, intimate, and smudged at the edges. A coarse halftone field floods the background, dissolving any imagery into constellations of oversized ink dots. The composition is asymmetric and anchor-low, with the title massed toward the bottom-left while a ghost offset layer drifts independently above it, embodying the productive misalignment of a second riso ink pass. Every surface should resist digital cleanliness — no smooth gradients, no crisp registration, nothing that could not plausibly have come out of a basement duplicator.

examples.layoutNotes: Loose 12-column grid with ~10% outer margins, but the halftone background field bleeds edge-to-edge on the right side, breaking the grid's authority. Title text occupies a left-anchored block in cols 1–7, positioned in the lower third of the slide, while a second riso-ink ghost layer carrying a duplicate or echo of the title drifts rightward and upward to simulate deliberate misregistration. A subtitle or author credit sits just below the title block, separated by a rough hand-drawn rule or smudged baseline rather than clean spacing. No header band; a small issue or chapbook number lives in the upper-right corner as a zine-artifact timestamp.

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a riso print pulled at 2 a.m. — two ink passes that never quite aligned, leaving a ghost shadow behind every letterform and a field of coarse halftone dots where a portrait or texture dissolves at the edge. Compositional rhythm is asymmetric: one dense, slightly smudged typographic pocket balanced against an expansive dot-screen field that breathes and erodes outward. The mood is intimate conviction — the kind carried inside a staple-bound chapbook passed hand-to-hand at a lit fair. Avoid all digital smoothness: no clean antialiasing, no gradient transitions, no vector crispness anywhere on the canvas.

examples.layoutNotes: Asymmetric 12-column grid; a pull quote or 3-line poem excerpt occupies cols 2–8, while a coarse halftone dot field bleeds off the right edge through cols 9–12. Attribution or section tag sits one row below the main text block, nudged a half-column left to simulate ink-drift misregistration. No header band; a zine folio numeral anchors the lower-left with tight outer margins on the text side and a near-bleed crop on the image side. Hierarchy is established through scale contrast and halftone density alone — no rule lines.
